```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
using CairoMakie, CEVE543Utils, CSV, DataFrames, Dates, Distributions, Printf, Statistics, Unitful

set_theme!(theme_minimal(); fontsize=20)
colors = Makie.wong_colors()

here = @__DIR__

# Least-squares slope of y on t
slope_of(t, y) = cov(t, y) / var(t)

# Regression slope with a two-sided t-test on beta_1 = 0
function slope_test(t, y)
    n = length(y)
    slope = slope_of(t, y)
    resid = y .- (mean(y) .+ slope .* (t .- mean(t)))
    se = sqrt(sum(resid .^ 2) / (n - 2) / sum((t .- mean(t)) .^ 2))
    return 2 * ccdf(TDist(n - 2), abs(slope / se))
end

# Mann-Kendall S, no-ties variance, continuity-corrected normal approximation
function mann_kendall(y)
    n = length(y)
    S = sum(sign(y[j] - y[i]) for i in 1:n for j in (i+1):n)
    Z = (S - sign(S)) / sqrt(n * (n - 1) * (2n + 5) / 18)
    return 2 * ccdf(Normal(), abs(Z))
end

fmt_p(p) = p < 0.001 ? "< 0.001" : @sprintf("%.2f", p)

# Hobby annual maximum daily rainfall, built by scripts/write_hobby.jl
hobby = CSV.read(joinpath(here, "hobby-annmax.csv"), DataFrame)
hobby = hobby[hobby.n_valid_days .>= 350, :]

# Brays Bayou annual peaks, USGS 08075000 (the week's reading)
brays_rows = [split(l, '\t') for l in readlines(joinpath(here, "08075000-peaks.tsv")) if !startswith(l, "#")][3:end]
brays_rows = filter(r -> !isempty(strip(r[5])), brays_rows)
brays_year = [parse(Int, r[3][1:4]) for r in brays_rows]
brays_peak = [parse(Float64, r[5]) for r in brays_rows]

# Annual maximum water levels, raw and with annual mean sea level subtracted (weeks 4 and 5)
sewells = load_water_level("8638610"; name="Sewells Point", cache=joinpath(here, "..", "..", "labs", "lab-04", "8638610-hourly.csv"))
galveston = load_water_level("8771450"; name="Galveston Pier 21", cache=joinpath(here, "..", "week-05", "8771450-hourly.csv"), first_year=1904)
annmax(record, detrend) = AnnMaxRecord(record; detrend=detrend, units=u"m")
series(record, detrend) = (obsyears(annmax(record, detrend)), ustrip.(waterlevels(annmax(record, detrend))))

records = [
    ("Hobby rainfall", hobby.year, hobby.prcp_mm),
    ("Brays Bayou peak flow", brays_year, brays_peak),
    ("Sewells Point water level", series(sewells, :none)...),
    ("... minus mean sea level", series(sewells, :msl)...),
    ("Galveston water level", series(galveston, :none)...),
    ("... minus mean sea level", series(galveston, :msl)...),
]
results = DataFrame(
    "Record" => [r[1] for r in records],
    "Years" => ["$(first(r[2]))-$(last(r[2]))" for r in records],
    "Regression p" => [fmt_p(slope_test(r[2], r[3])) for r in records],
    "Mann-Kendall p" => [fmt_p(mann_kendall(r[3])) for r in records],
)

# Hobby daily rainfall, restricted to the same complete years as the annual maxima
daily_all = CSV.read(joinpath(here, "hobby-daily.csv"), DataFrame)
daily = filter(r -> year(r.date) in Set(hobby.year), daily_all)

# Storms above 2 inches over 1947-2025, where every year has at least 334 days;
# rainy days within 3 days of each other are one storm
storm_threshold = 50.8
span = filter(r -> Date(1947) <= r.date <= Date(2025, 12, 31), daily_all)
storm_idx, _ = decluster_daily(span.prcp_mm, storm_threshold; min_gap_days=3)
storm_date = span.date[storm_idx]
storm_peak = span.prcp_mm[storm_idx]
storm_year = year.(storm_date)
storm_decimal_year = [year(d) + (dayofyear(d) - 1) / 365.25 for d in storm_date]
storms_per_year = [count(==(y), storm_year) for y in 1947:2025]
days_between = Dates.value.(diff(storm_date))

# Slope on the annual maxima, as a size rather than a p-value
amax_slope = slope_of(hobby.year, hobby.prcp_mm)
amax_change = amax_slope * (last(hobby.year) - first(hobby.year))
```

## Null hypothesis significance testing

::: {.incremental}
1. State a **null hypothesis** $H_0$, such as "no trend"
1. Choose a **test statistic**
1. Work out (derive or simulate) the statistic's distribution **if $H_0$ were true**
1. Compare the observed statistic to that distribution
:::

::: {.fragment}
The **p-value** is the probability, if $H_0$ were true, of a statistic at least as extreme as the one observed.

- A small p-value means data like these would be unusual under $H_0$.
- Reject $H_0$ when the p-value is below a level chosen in advance, usually 0.05.
:::

## What a p-value is not

- A p-value is $P(\text{data this extreme} \mid H_0)$.
- It is **not** $P(H_0 \mid \text{data})$, such as the probability that there is no trend [@serinaldi_untenablenonstationarity:2018, p. 136].
- A large p-value does not show that $H_0$ is true.

## Side rant

A p-value is useful when interpreted carefully.
The trouble comes from treating a hypothesis as simply true or false, and sorting effects into "real" and "not real".
For more, read:

- @mcshane_abandonsignificance:2017
- @gelman_subjectiveobjective:2017
- @stark_cargo-cultstatistics:2018
- @gelman_philosophy:2013

## The regression slope test

- Fit $y_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 t + \varepsilon_t$ by least squares; test $\beta_1 = 0$ with a $t$ statistic.
- Assumes independent, normal residuals with constant variance.

## The Mann-Kendall test

- $S = \sum_{i < j} \operatorname{sign}(y_j - y_i)$: pairs where the later value is larger, minus pairs where it is smaller.
- Under $H_0$ (independent, identically distributed years, no ties), $S$ is approximately normal with mean 0 and variance $n(n-1)(2n+5)/18$.
- Uses only the ordering, so it assumes no distribution for $y$.

## Trend tests on records we have seen

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println("| Record | Years | Regression p | Mann-Kendall p |")
println("| :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: |")
for r in eachrow(results)
    println("| ", join(r, " | "), " |")
end
```

"... minus mean sea level" subtracts each year's mean water level before taking the maximum, as in week 5.
For supplementary notes on both tests, read @helsel_waterresources:2020 §12.2, pp. 332-336.

## Reading the table

- Both coastal records reject "no trend", and neither does once mean sea level is subtracted.
- Brays Bayou rejects; Hobby does not.

::: {.callout-tip .pause}
## Think

If we already know the cause, what did the test add?

## Daily rainfall at Hobby

```{julia}
#| echo: false
fig = Figure(; size=(1000, 170))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1]; xlabel="Date", ylabel="Daily rainfall (mm)")
scatter!(ax, daily.date, daily.prcp_mm; color=colors[1], markersize=3)
hlines!(ax, [storm_threshold]; color=colors[2], linestyle=:dash)
fig
```

`{julia} length(storm_peak)` storms above 2 inches (dashed) from 1947 to 2025, counting rainy days within 3 days of each other as one storm.

## Four things that could be changing at Hobby

```{julia}
#| echo: false
fig = Figure(; size=(1100, 560))
panels = [
    ("Largest day each year (mm)", hobby.year, hobby.prcp_mm),
    ("Storms per year", collect(1947:2025), storms_per_year),
    ("Largest day of each storm (mm)", storm_decimal_year, storm_peak),
    ("Days since the previous storm", storm_decimal_year[2:end], days_between),
]
for (k, (label, t, y)) in enumerate(panels)
    ax = Axis(fig[fldmod1(k, 2)...]; title="$label: Mann-Kendall p = $(fmt_p(mann_kendall(y)))", titlesize=18)
    scatter!(ax, t, y; color=colors[1], markersize=5)
end
fig
```

## A slope can be large and not significant

- Hobby's annual maxima rise `{julia} @sprintf("%.2f", amax_slope)` mm per year, with p = `{julia} fmt_p(slope_test(hobby.year, hobby.prcp_mm))`.
- That is `{julia} round(Int, amax_change)` mm over `{julia} last(hobby.year) - first(hobby.year)` years, `{julia} round(Int, 100amax_change / mean(hobby.prcp_mm))`% of the average annual maximum.

::: {.callout-tip .pause}

## Two nearby rivers with a step change around 1975

![Average annual discharge, 1916-2015, for two rivers the authors call the Nera and the Velino [@serinaldi_untenablenonstationarity:2018, Fig. 1a-b, CC BY 4.0].](serinaldi-fig1-rivers.png){width=100%}

Every change-point test rejects "no change" for both [@serinaldi_untenablenonstationarity:2018, p. 133].

## Neither series is a river

![The "Nera" is independent noise plus a step; the "Velino" is a window, in the red box, of a stationary process with long memory [@serinaldi_untenablenonstationarity:2018, Fig. 1i-j, CC BY 4.0].](serinaldi-fig1-reveal.png){width=100%}

## Memory alone makes Mann-Kendall reject

Annual maximum flow at 250 US streamflow gauges [@serinaldi_untenablenonstationarity:2018, pp. 147-148]:

- standard Mann-Kendall rejects "no trend" at 46;
- a null that keeps each river's memory rejects at 12;
- chance alone, at the 5% level, gives about 12.
